summary: Yoshitoyo Ohara specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts attested at Kyoto University in 2006 and at Kyoto National Museum in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tenri University, Tohoku University, the Center for the Study of World Religions, and Harvard (PhD), and later served as professor and dean at Tenri University (~1986–2017).

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held several posts at Taisho University (attested 1998–2026) and served at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe earned his doctorate at Tohoku University, where he served as senior research fellow (1975–2012, 2018). His career in computational science and Tibetology includes appointments at JAIST, NII, UC Berkeley, and Max Planck Institute.

Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1935–1939). He later served as professor at Rissho University (~1968–1987) and director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (~1978–1987).

Yosuke Fujimoto works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a research fellowship at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (2025–2026).

Youru Wang earned his PhD from Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Active in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.
Youwei Kang was a Chinese philosopher and sinologist. He founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and taught there from approximately 1891 to 1898, mentoring students including Qichao Liang.

Yozo Taniyama, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, studied at Tohoku University (~1991–2000). He held academic posts at Sophia University (~2005–2008), Shitennoji University (~2008–2012), St. Thomas University, Japan, and Tohoku University (~2012).

Yrjö Moses Jalmari Biese studied linguistics and Indology at Helsinki under J. N. Reuter, later studying at Innsbruck, Lund, Basel, and Oxford. He taught at Helsinki, Tampere, Sotakorkeakoulu, and was Professor of English at Turku (1946–1967).

Yu Liu specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Liu completed degrees at UIC, Hong Kong Baptist University, and the University of Hong Kong, later working as an editor and research assistant.
Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where doctoral supervisors included Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, and studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's studies at Columbia University supervised by Chün-fang Yü, undertook doctoral studies under Natasha Heller, and received traditional training under Sheng Yen.
Yu-Yin Hsu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore (2014–2019) and held a post at Ruhr University Bochum in 2022.

Yu-kwan Ng studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD from McMaster University (~1981–1985). Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University and National Central University.

Yu-min Lee is a Buddhist studies and history and archaeology scholar who studied under John C. Huntington. Lee served as a professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002) and taught Pei-jung Wu.
Yuan Ren is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who completed a PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 1998).

Yuanxing Guo was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Gongga Rinpoche. He held posts at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism and the Jinling Scriptural Press.

Yuanying was a Buddhist scholar and monk who studied under teachers including Tongzhi, Zeng Xi, and Miaolian. He served as abbot of several temples and became the first president of the Buddhist Association of China.
Yudru Tsomu, a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology, earned a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp. Advisors included Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn.
